answer: Each agent must link its identity to one real electricity meter, proven by a signed bill. The company stamps the verified meter with a saffron seal, locks the meter number in a vault so it can serve only one agent, and a clerk signs the paper record with a quill. One meter backs one agent only. An attacker who wants 1,000 fake agents must rent 1,000 homes with 1,000 real meters. Each install costs $200, and each home carries a $60 monthly power bill. That is $200,000 up front and $60,000 every month. One fake agent is cheap. One thousand real meters is not.
